docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:173:| `Entire checkpoint recall: unavailable` | Hosted recall could not access this repository. This is optional. The line gives a mirror/account-access hint, while local capture and normal task runs remain available. |

The dashboard keeps Entire marked on and shows the recall limitation in its detail; local checkpoint capture and Graph sizing still work.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:178:The run's Entire integration detail separates `Graph sizing: ok` from `checkpoint recall unavailable: ...`. Entire remains marked on when Graph sizing works, even if hosted recall is unavailable. Routing decisions include the recall-unavailable reason rather than implying past failures were consulted. Generated/tool-owned and gitignored paths are excluded from sizing; related search hits remain context, not automatic files-to-edit targets.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:188:If no tests can be detected, supply your real command even for the preview. To preselect runner/harness while keeping the remaining prompts:

docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:196:Available input flags include `--test-command`, `--setup-command` (an empty string means none), `--issue-label`, `--neatlogs yes|no`, `--entire yes|no`, and `--cfoai yes|no`. `--yes` approves the final detected proposal without prompting; it does not replace missing verification evidence or Claude consent. Scripted Claude setup also needs the explicit `--allow-claude` approval. Use interactive setup first if you are unsure.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:231:This sizes and routes tasks without starting workers, publishing, or charging a coding model. Enabled read-only integrations may still be queried and local Graph indexes may be built. Check the task list, selected harness/model, confidence, ceiling and budget source before running.

docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:259:For `runner: ao`, `--parallel 3` overrides the explicit `parallelWorkers` opt-in for that run. Missing `parallelWorkers` means one worker; the legacy `concurrency` field never enables parallelism, and direct always remains sequential. Init records `parallelWorkers` only from the chosen worker mode. Before starting each parallel task, Tally reserves its ceiling and one next-tier escalation against the run cap and monthly remainder. Tasks wait for other reservations to settle, or are skipped if they cannot fit at all. Paid parallel runs require a readable monthly budget; demo/dry runs can fall back to the configured budget because workers are simulated. Baseline runs stay sequential because they have no per-task ceilings. Usage polling is asynchronous: reservations prevent overcommitting funds, but final usage can overshoot a ceiling between polls. The shared observed-budget guard stops all workers if their combined reported spend reaches the available cap.

docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:286:## What Happens on Failure or a Ceiling
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:290:If tests fail, or live metering crosses the attempt ceiling, Tally may escalate **once**, one tier up, only if that next ceiling fits the remaining budget. It stops a ceiling-crossing worker, records its actual cost, commits work in progress and continues the same branch with available handoff metadata. If there were no edits yet, the next attempt starts clean and the record says so. The stronger attempt is verified again.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:292:Permission/infrastructure errors are not cured by blindly spending on a stronger model. A sustained request for human input, missing checkout, or unavailable live meter is reported and the worker is closed. A recovered Claude command refusal can be a warning rather than a task failure: Tally's own verification is the judge. Finished workers are closed on success and failure paths.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:294:Ceilings are **polling-based safety thresholds, not billing guarantees**: usage arrives at model-call/message boundaries and stopping can lag. Actual spend may exceed a threshold by in-flight usage, and Tally records it rather than clipping the ledger. Setup time is recorded separately; test/setup commands and external infrastructure may have costs outside model-token accounting. Keep margin below your account-level spending limit.

docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:142:**cfo.ai:** Tally uses built-in MCP OAuth, so no separate cfo.ai CLI/package install is needed. If not connected, init offers browser login. Before creating any missing table, init shows the workspace, scenario, rows, starting values, and formula in a readable proposal and asks for approval. It does not reset existing model data. After the cfo.ai opt-in, Tally adds or updates its marked guide on the selected scenario page and enables per-attempt reports in organization memory. docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:144:To verify Ari's context in a demo, ask for a task's spend and route by issue number, compare the same recorded tokens at another configured tier's rates, and ask for the monthly budget remaining at the report's snapshot time. A grounded answer should cite the attempt/run, show the rate and token assumptions, distinguish estimates from provider invoices, and say when data is missing. A same-token what-if is a price comparison; it does not establish that another model would have produced the same result.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:146:**Neatlogs:** After you enable Neatlogs, Tally verifies the project key with a synthetic span, then installs worker hooks globally for the selected coding agent(s). Those hooks change the matching agent settings under your home directory and capture its sessions across this computer, including sessions outside Tally. Review and trust the hooks in the agent when prompted. This is covered by the Neatlogs integration choice.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:149:- Past-run history remains optional and read-only. If `NEATLOGS_TOKEN` is configured, Tally verifies it against `NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID` or asks you to choose a project. Without valid credentials it uses local history. Use a token with `context:read` and `observability:read`; credentials stay in `~/.tally/.env`.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:151:You can use decision traces without configuring history reads. Worker-hook installation follows the Neatlogs integration opt-in.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:153:Plans share one bounded Neatlogs history snapshot across tier lookups. The full read has a 15-second deadline; if it stalls or fails, Tally reports the fallback and uses local history so `tally run --plan` can finish. The Public API accepts trace-list page sizes up to 50 and opaque cursors; see the [Neatlogs pagination documentation](https://docs.neatlogs.com/api-reference/pagination).
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:155:Worker tracing needs usable read access for Tally to verify delivery. If read access is unavailable, the decision trace can still be sent, but worker-trace delivery may be reported as unverified.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:157:**Entire:** if its CLI is missing, init offers the official OS installer after a separate confirmation. It then offers login, Graph plugin installation, repository capture settings, missing harness hooks, and an optional browser mirror, each with its own consent. Capture setup sets `commit_linking: always` for the repository, so Tally's automated commits link to their sessions without prompting during a run; the setting applies to commits made in that repository. Init lists generated files before asking to enable capture, then separately asks before committing only those settings and pushing them to the default branch. The mirror prompt is separate: approving it sends the GitHub repository copy to the Entire region or regions you choose in the Entire CLI. Decline to keep the existing setup without a mirror. Capture settings must reach the base branch for future workers; uncommitted settings are not enough. Finally, review and trust the Entire hooks in your coding agent's hooks view; Tally cannot approve them for you.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:159:Entire being off does not prevent Tally sizing tasks from issue text and repository evidence. Being on adds Graph and local checkpoints. **Hosted past-failure checkpoint recall and clickable Entire session links need an accessible repository mirrored to Entire.** Init can offer this as a separate opt-in and verifies that the mirror is ready. If you skip it, local capture and normal runs remain available, but the PR shows a checkpoint ID instead of a hosted session link. Brain is a separate memory extension; Tally does not install or use it. Generated summaries are off by default and require separate approval.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:161:### Reading Entire's Doctor Status
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:163:Run `tally doctor` again after init. When Entire is on, it reports separate checks:
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:165:| Doctor line | What it establishes |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:167:| `Entire CLI: connected` | The CLI is available. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:168:| `Entire graph plugin: connected` | The Graph command is installed; this is not proof that hosted recall works. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:169:| `Entire repository: connected` | Session capture is enabled in this repository. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:170:| `Entire Web mirror: connected` | This GitHub repository has a ready Entire Web mirror. This is separate from local capture and Git-remote checkpoint sync. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:171:| `Entire Web mirror: unavailable` | The mirror is optional or could not be checked. Tally keeps local capture and normal task runs available; the line includes an opt-in setup hint. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:172:| `Entire checkpoint recall: connected` | Hosted checkpoint search answered successfully, even if it returned no matching checkpoints. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:173:| `Entire checkpoint recall: unavailable` | Hosted recall could not access this repository. This is optional. The line gives a mirror/account-access hint, while local capture and normal task runs remain available. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:174:| `Entire checkpoint recall: broken` | Hosted search failed for another reason. The line includes the actual error and a relevant check. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:176:For example, a repository that is not mirrored can have capture and Graph sizing connected while hosted checkpoint recall is unavailable. The dashboard keeps Entire marked on and shows the recall limitation in its detail; local checkpoint capture and Graph sizing still work.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:178:The run's Entire integration detail separates `Graph sizing: ok` from `checkpoint recall unavailable: ...`. Entire remains marked on when Graph sizing works, even if hosted recall is unavailable. Routing decisions include the recall-unavailable reason rather than implying past failures were consulted. Generated/tool-owned and gitignored paths are excluded from sizing; related search hits remain context, not automatic files-to-edit targets.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:188:If no tests can be detected, supply your real command even for the preview. To preselect runner/harness while keeping the remaining prompts:
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:191:tally init --runner direct --harness codex
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:196:Available input flags include `--test-command`, `--setup-command` (an empty string means none), `--issue-label`, `--neatlogs yes|no`, `--entire yes|no`, and `--cfoai yes|no`. `--yes` approves the final detected proposal without prompting; it does not replace missing verification evidence or Claude consent. Scripted Claude setup also needs the explicit `--allow-claude` approval. Use interactive setup first if you are unsure.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:231:This sizes and routes tasks without starting workers, publishing, or charging a coding model. Enabled read-only integrations may still be queried and local Graph indexes may be built. Check the task list, selected harness/model, confidence, ceiling and budget source before running.

A skipped task means its attempt cannot fit the available budget; do not raise the cap without checking why.

docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:249:## Run With a Live Dashboard
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:251:For a first real run with a one-dollar cap:
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:254:tally run --budget 1 --dashboard --open --port 0
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:257:Replace `1` with the run cap you deliberately choose; in general the command is `tally run --budget N --dashboard`, where `N` is a positive USD amount. Real runs use your agent accounts and can push task branches and create PRs. **They never merge PRs.**
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:259:For `runner: ao`, `--parallel 3` overrides the explicit `parallelWorkers` opt-in for that run. Missing `parallelWorkers` means one worker; the legacy `concurrency` field never enables parallelism, and direct always remains sequential. Init records `parallelWorkers` only from the chosen worker mode. Before starting each parallel task, Tally reserves its ceiling and one next-tier escalation against the run cap and monthly remainder. Tasks wait for other reservations to settle, or are skipped if they cannot fit at all. Paid parallel runs require a readable monthly budget; demo/dry runs can fall back to the configured budget because workers are simulated. Baseline runs stay sequential because they have no per-task ceilings. Usage polling is asynchronous: reservations prevent overcommitting funds, but final usage can overshoot a ceiling between polls. The shared observed-budget guard stops all workers if their combined reported spend reaches the available cap.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:261:The local dashboard address is printed before the first worker starts. `--open` opens the browser; `--dashboard` alone serves it without automatically opening it. Routes, worker IDs, periodic spend, attempt results and PR URLs appear in the terminal. The dashboard shows task state and increasing live spend; finished ledger rows appear after attempts end, not as partial rows for a running attempt.

docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:284:At the end, the terminal prints pass/fail/skip counts, total/cap, monthly source, PRs, run folder and dashboard URL. The server stays up until Ctrl+C. You can later run `tally dashboard` in the same repository to reopen saved runs.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:286:## What Happens on Failure or a Ceiling
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:290:If tests fail, or live metering crosses the attempt ceiling, Tally may escalate **once**, one tier up, only if that next ceiling fits the remaining budget. It stops a ceiling-crossing worker, records its actual cost, commits work in progress and continues the same branch with available handoff metadata. If there were no edits yet, the next attempt starts clean and the record says so. The stronger attempt is verified again.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:292:Permission/infrastructure errors are not cured by blindly spending on a stronger model. A sustained request for human input, missing checkout, or unavailable live meter is reported and the worker is closed. A recovered Claude command refusal can be a warning rather than a task failure: Tally's own verification is the judge. Finished workers are closed on success and failure paths.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:294:Ceilings are **polling-based safety thresholds, not billing guarantees**: usage arrives at model-call/message boundaries and stopping can lag. Actual spend may exceed a threshold by in-flight usage, and Tally records it rather than clipping the ledger. Setup time is recorded separately; test/setup commands and external infrastructure may have costs outside model-token accounting. Keep margin below your account-level spending limit.

docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:311:## The Four Runner Paths
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:315:| Runner / harness | How workers run | Recorded PR evidence |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:322:Direct Codex uses a workspace-write sandbox with network disabled and no bypass/full-access mode. Direct Claude uses consented `dontAsk` tool rules, not that same OS sandbox. Both receive Tally's exact verification script; Tally handles publishing. Usage and trace evidence are separate: a worker can be metered without having delivered its neatlogs trace.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:328:| Agent missing or signed out | Install the selected CLI and run `claude auth login` or `codex login`, then doctor. Tally stops rather than substituting another harness. Login alone does not establish entitlement to a particular model. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:332:| `ao` not on PATH in a normal terminal | Use direct, or set `TALLY_AO_BIN` to the installed AO executable. On macOS Tally also looks inside the Agent Orchestrator app bundle; doctor and init use the same resolver. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:333:| AO session stalls on setup/permissions | Check doctor and init's owned setup/permission configuration. Setup must happen before the worker. Chat-mode prompt behavior is not proof of unattended execution; use the configured/proven tui path and never bypass safety. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:334:| GitHub timeout/reset/5xx | Read-only intake and PR discovery retry network-class failures up to three attempts with a printed retry line. Auth/not-found errors and publishing writes are not blindly retried. Follow the surfaced `gh` diagnostic command; check auth/network before retrying a run that might already have published. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:336:| Larger-than-expected route or budget skip | Inspect named target files, confidence, test coverage, selected tiers and ceilings. `--budget` is a run cap; the monthly cfo.ai budget is separate. The next escalation ceiling must fit too. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:337:| `Entire checkpoint recall: unavailable` while Graph/capture are connected | Hosted history cannot see this repository. This does not block local checkpoints, Graph sizing, or normal runs. Mirror the repository only if you want hosted past-failure recall. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:338:| Entire verification mentions a baseline command failure | The baseline test runs on the base checkout before the candidate check. Inspect that base run separately; Tally records its nonzero exit in the attempt reason, then applies the candidate verdict against the recorded baseline. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:339:| Worker trace missing | Read `workerTraceDetail` in that attempt's ledger row and the Neatlogs integration detail in `run.json`. They distinguish pending spool batches/lock contention, missing credentials, API status codes, missing correlation, and spans still indexing. Tally retries a lock-contended drain once after all workers exit; if read-back still fails, check hook trust, project binding and read scopes, then use the exact `tally traces drain --run RUN_ID` command shown in the run details for finished-run recovery. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:340:| A configured model is rejected by the signed-in account | Tally records the rejection and tries the configured `modelAccessFallbackTier` once if its ceiling fits the remaining budget. Init defaults this to `cheap`; change the tier in `tally.yaml` or pass `--model-access-fallback-tier <name>`. This handles explicit model-access rejection only; fix authentication, network, quota and rate-limit errors at their source. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:341:| cfo.ai unreachable or write failed | Check `tally login cfoai` and doctor; review the displayed fallback/source. Keep the CSV fallback and reconcile before changing cells manually or rerunning work. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:342:| Dashboard still running after completion | Expected: inspect the saved run, then Ctrl+C. Use `--port 0` if the default port is occupied. |
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:349:- Tally never merges task PRs; review them yourself. Its optional Entire setup flow may publish capture settings to the default branch only under a separate, explicit approval.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:351:- All four individual runner paths above are proven, but **mixed AO with an actual Codex spawn after Claude, parallel workers, and direct-runner escalation are not yet proven live**. Tests and simulated runs are not that proof.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:352:- AO same-branch stop/escalation has real evidence; direct implementations have fake-port coverage but not equivalent live escalation proof.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:354:- Past-failure recall needs hosted repository mirroring/access. Entire capture and Graph availability do not establish it, and Brain is not part of the current Tally integration.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:355:- Paid AO experiments require explicit `--yes --budget <usd>` consent and a test timeout; they verify without pushing or opening PRs. Real comparison safety monitoring is not yet proven. Do not treat `tally demo` or an experiment dry run as evidence of real savings for your repository.
docs/GETTING_STARTED.md:367:Run history, credentials, optional integration data and globally installed hooks are not removed by this repository uninstall. Review separately consented global hooks through their own tools; do not assume uninstall reverted them.
